summary.title: hecto: Build Your Own Text Editor in Rust
summary.one_liner: You learn Rust by building a minimal terminal text editor step by step, with search and syntax highlighting, as a re-implementation of antirez's kilo.
keywords: how to write a text editor in rust
takeaways: Build a text editor of roughly 3000 lines of Rust across a few files with a few dependencies.
Follow chapters covering setup, entering raw mode, raw input and output, a text viewer, a text editor, search, and syntax highlighting.
Learn Rust through small incremental code changes, with compile-and-run checks after most steps.
Use it as a remix of Paige Ruten's C tutorial and a re-implementation of antirez's kilo.
summary.summary: This is the introduction to a blog-post tutorial series in which the author builds a minimal text editor in Rust. The editor is a re-implementation of antirez's kilo and a remix of Paige Ruten's C tutorial, roughly 3000 lines of Rust. The series is organized into chapters from setup and raw terminal mode through a text viewer, editing, search, and syntax highlighting. Readers are encouraged to type in the code step by step, with optional prose and assignments for those who want to solve problems themselves.
